rationale.conceptual: Uses non-trivial but established methods: GCMC adsorption with Ewald summation, MD with protein flexibility, and post-analysis like MSD power-law fitting. Requires careful force field choices and simulation parameters; no novel algorithm but multi-part documented procedure.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline: box building, porosity, GCMC adsorption, hydration shell analysis, GCMC desorption, isotherm compilation, MD simulations (rigid+flexible), MSD calculation, exponent fitting, lattice parameter extraction. Fragile handoffs between GCMC and MD, multiple tools (GROMACS, RASPA2) and file formats; overall 9+ sequential steps with load-bearing handoffs.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper requires standard molecular simulation techniques (GCMC and MD) using established force fields, but correct setup, protonation, and multi-step analysis (adsorption, desorption, hydration shell, MSD fitting) make it moderately complex conceptually. The execution pipeline involves multiple tools (GROMACS, RASPA2) and many stages (construction, GCMC, MD, post-processing) making it a heavy orchestration task.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Modest system size (~8 proteins, a few thousand water molecules) allows CPU-only simulation; MD 5.5 ns can be done on a single CPU in hours; GCMC cycles similar; data (PDB, force field files) is tiny.
